logline: An engagement is broken off as a temple decays: the tambourine that was the ring of the promise sounds through an empty church, a storm turns love into ruined goods, and two sets of footprints leave while the tambourine shatters.
reading:
The poem is an inverted wedding liturgy. Each 'Ode' (read aloud as 'Old to', so the praise already sounds aged) is sung to a ceremony that never happened. The temple, choir stands, prayer lines and baptism pools are all empty. The pews are wrapped in cobwebs, the gift boxes are opened and left outside the side doors, the spirits have gone. The tambourine is the church's music and also a ring of jingles: the engagement itself, still whole as it flies through the empty space.

The turn is 'Old to the storm ending, what was once love now goods,'. After it the poem stops mourning a place and counts what is left of two lives, as a ledger: goods sealed apart by lightning, daily bread rotted by rain, blankets soiled by 'venomous puppeteers', a nod to the hands that worked the couple, and to our own rods and strings. It ends small and exact: two sets of button-printed footsteps, out of step, and the tambourine shattered into pieces.
motifs: the tambourine as ring: whole, suspended, shattered
emptiness counted in a list: temple, choir stands, prayer lines, pools
wedding gifts opened and left at the side door
daily bread soaked and rotted: shared domestic life spoiled
puppeteers and cut strings: who worked the couple
two sets of button-printed footsteps, out of step
time-lapse decay: cobweb, dust, varnish flaking
lightning as the knife that seals things apart

light_and_texture: Begin warm and gilded (amber glass, dust in shafts), then drain to cold grey through the time-lapse, with lightning as hard white single frames cut into the corrugation. The cardboard should age on camera: pew and choir cards get progressively scuffed kraft edges, cobwebs drawn in white pencil on tracing paper laid over them, and the gift boxes and bread as clean gouache cards that are swapped for water-stained, buckled versions (really wet the card and let it cockle). Rain is scratched into black acetate, kept above the cards, and the mud shore is a sheet of brown kraft dragged with grey wash.

gaps: A figure-free chapel interior with choir stands, kneelers and a dry baptism pool: G0 is all window, so the nave itself is missing.
The shore after the storm with the chapel actually in ruins (pew ends, lead tracery, a cross half-sunk): gen_e315da34f9 still shows the chapel standing.
A hero tambourine card with jingles: every generated version is a lugged frame drum. It needs whole, cracked and shattered states that carry into 04.
Painted poet back-walk and EX back-walk cards: the black_tshirt and ex_jacket packs are blank layouts.
The opened white gift box glowing on the stone step: no generated or archive frame shows it on a doorstep.
The 'button-printed footsteps': nothing shows prints made of buttons, so it needs a stamped-card insert.
Archive rain and flooding on a church or house interior; current rain is all sky or glass.
A clear time-lapse of cobweb or dust accumulation: Spider Engineers is close-up web only.

fx.how: Rotate the tambourine card on a single centre brad and swap in a smear card on every third frame; jingle glints on a separate acetate layer.
Lock the plate and dissolve through three painted decay states of each card (clean, cobwebbed, rotted) while code races a light gradient across the floor.
White-pencil webs on tracing paper revealed row by row with a code wipe mask.
Code-drawn particles in the window shafts, with a warm tint before the storm and grey after.
Two or three single-frame cuts to a violet-white flash with a black silhouette card of the chapel; borrow the timing from Lightning 3 (2007).
Scratched black acetate scrolled diagonally over everything, plus real rain-on-glass (gen_dd0782d25a) as a cutaway.
Swap the whole tambourine for its pieces in one frame, then throw each piece card on a short code-driven arc; jingles bounce twice.
A radial gradient behind each opened gift box card that fades out over the time-lapse: the salvations leaving.
Slide the plate's sky up and dissolve to gen_bb8e6e2acf / the clearing marsh light; a last-rain acetate thins out.

passage.keep: The hand that opens and stays open is the right gesture for 'daily breads soaked and delivered rotted': he shows what is left, which is nothing. The Gardening (1940) answer 'Rain, rain, it's soaked into the water' gives the same rain as both ruin and nourishment.
passage.better: Move the surface from the rain pool (water reads faint) to an upright salvaged door_frame card standing in the mud beside the pool, so the film opens in a vertical pane and reflects down into the water. Crop gen_e315da34f9 so the chapel's own arched doorway is large if no card is built. Put a soaked loaf card on the ground under his open palm, and swap his head to 'down' on the archive line.

03_L08 'blankets soiled by venomous puppeteers': a grip on cut marionette strings; World of Tomorrow (Part II) marionette shadows open in the chapel door arch of gen_933cc247ea.

ideas: Ring rhyme: For Health and Happiness (1941), the ringed hand slicing loaves, plays in a pane while the bread card on the altar step swells and rots in time-lapse. The engagement ring is in the archive and its ruin is in paper.

The empty hall: Het crematorium Westerveld (1925) is cut in as a straight archive shot between gen_872d16167d and the choir-stand card. Its rows of empty seats are the 'empty prayer lines', with no puppet in the shot.

Puppeteers revealed: in 03.4d a cut-out cross-bar control descends into frame on real black thread over the blanket card, while World of Tomorrow (Part II) marionette shadows play on the chapel wall. The poem's 'venomous puppeteers' are our own rig.
Lightning cut: the gift box card splits in two on a single flash frame lifted from Lightning 3 (2007), and the halves stay apart for the rest of the scene.
Gifts at the door: gen_09d9df4ac6 as plate, three opened gift box cards on the step with a fading glow, and Consumers Want to Know (1960) visible inside the nearest box like a diorama.
Button-printed footsteps: two sneaker cards press prints one at a time into kraft mud, one trail stamped with buttons; then wide on gen_e948110f1d as the two back-view figures walk out of step.
Shatter bridge to 04: the tambourine lands in gen_2bd9f63a13's light pool and bursts. The pieces' arc carries to the waterline, where 04 opens on the same pieces.
Blankets: Duck and Cover (1951), figures under blankets on bare ground, plays inside the door_frame card while the muddy blanket card lies at its foot.
